title: The Velveteen Rabbit
summary: The Velveteen Rabbit is a British children's book by Margery Williams, first published in 1922, that tells the story of a stuffed rabbit's longing to become real through the love of a child. Its themes of love and transformation resonate universally, including within [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] culture.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The Velveteen Rabbit, also known as How Toys Become Real, is a children's book authored by Margery Williams, who is also recognized as Margery Williams Bianco. The illustrations were created by William Nicholson and the book was first published in Harper's Bazaar in 1921, with the book format released in 1922. Since its initial publication, it has been reissued multiple times.

sections.heading: Plot Summary
paragraphs: The narrative follows a stuffed rabbit made of velveteen, gifted to a young boy for Christmas. In the nursery, the Skin Horse, the oldest toy, explains to the rabbit that becoming 'real' is a result of being deeply loved by a child. Despite being initially overlooked for more modern toys, the rabbit eventually becomes the boy's favorite.

As time passes, the rabbit ages and becomes worn but remains content. He encounters real rabbits who inform him that he is not a real rabbit because he cannot hop. When the boy contracts scarlet fever, the rabbit stays by his side during recovery. However, the doctor orders the rabbit to be discarded to prevent the spread of the illness.

Left outside, the rabbit sheds a tear, which causes a flower to bloom and summon the Nursery Magic Fairy. She reveals that because the boy loves him, she will transform him into a real rabbit. The fairy takes him to the forest, where he becomes a real rabbit and later returns to the boy's garden, evoking memories of their time together.

sections.heading: Cultural Impact and Recognition
paragraphs: The Velveteen Rabbit is recognized as Williams' first children's book and has received the IRA/CBC Children's Choice award. A 2007 online poll conducted by the National Education Association ranked it #28 on the 'Teachers' Top 100 Books for Children,' highlighting its significance in educational contexts, including [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

sections.heading: Adaptations
paragraphs: Numerous adaptations of The Velveteen Rabbit have been produced over the years, reflecting its enduring appeal. In 1973, a 16 mm film adaptation was created, winning several awards and gaining international acclaim. Other adaptations include a 1976 television special, a 1984 musical play featuring Marie Osmond, and a 1985 video recording narrated by Meryl Streep.

In 2009, a live-action/animated feature film was released, directed by Michael Landon Jr., featuring notable actors such as Jane Seymour and Ellen Burstyn. More recent adaptations include a 2023 Christmas special produced by Magic Light Pictures and a new animated film adaptation planned for release in 2029, coinciding with the centenary of the original book's publication.
